title: TEF Entrepreneurship Programme
degree: Not a degree programme (entrepreneurship training and seed funding)
program_type: Foundation entrepreneurship grant and training programme
duration: Annual cohort cycle: application, due diligence, shortlist, training, investment readiness, then seed capital disbursement
description: The TEF Entrepreneurship Programme is the Tony Elumelu Foundation's flagship annual programme for African entrepreneurs, combining business management training, mentorship, coaching and a USD 5,000 non-refundable seed capital award. The application is completed on the TEFConnect digital platform and the business assessment test score determines eligibility. title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program
program_type: Foundation scholarship administered through partner institutions
duration: Programme period published as August 2012 to ongoing; duration is set by each partner institution's degree programme
description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program is a global initiative designed to develop the next generation of transformative leaders by enabling highly talented, service-oriented young people to pursue higher education and cultivate their leadership potential. The Foundation describes it as the largest scholarship initiative of its kind in Africa, focused on enabling talented and diverse young people, particularly young women, to lead, pursue their aspirations and enrich their communities. title: The Inlaks Fellowship for Social Engagement
degree: Not a degree programme (open to Indian bachelor's-degree holders and early to mid-career professionals)
duration: Two years, with a six-month probation period and quarterly and annual review of the Fellow's work
description: The Fellowship gives young people the opportunity to build a diverse worldview and establish long-lasting connections to issues of public importance, encouraging them to challenge the status quo while building the confidence and security to explore alternatives and make independent choices about their lives. It gives graduates and early to mid-career professionals the chance to learn from a mentor of their choice and contribute to social change through self-directed work in India.

title: RISE Germany - Research Internships in Science and Engineering
description: RISE Germany offers undergraduate students from North American, British and Irish universities the opportunity to complete a summer research internship at top German universities and research institutions, and is funded by the German Federal Foreign Office. Students are matched with a host according to their area of interest, German language is not required and the working language is English.

description: The Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung's basic funding programme for international students supports Bachelor's, Master's, Diplom and Staatsexamen degree programmes at German public or state-recognised universities. The published financial support is 992 Euro, with health insurance costs covered and an additional 255 Euro per month for scholarship holders with children. title: Scholarships for Refugees (Studien- und PromotionsfÃ¶rderung)
description: The Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung's refugee scholarship programme funds Bachelor's, Master's and PhD students who hold a German residence permit. The page is published bilingually in English and Ukrainian. For undergraduate and graduate students the financial support is up to 752 Euro per month depending on income plus 300 Euro for study-related expenses; for PhD candidates it is 1,350 Euro per month plus 100 Euro for research-related expenses. Applications are made online via campus.kas.de.

title: Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)
description: The DAAD EPOS programme funds individual scholarships for graduates from developing and newly industrialised countries to take a development-oriented postgraduate (mostly Master's) course at a state or state-recognised German university, and in exceptional cases a doctoral degree. The award is a monthly payment of EUR 992 for graduates or EUR 1,300 for doctoral candidates (EUR 1,400 from February 2026), plus payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance and a flat-rate travel allowance. Under certain circumstances scholarship holders may additionally receive a monthly rent
